item.title: Place-Based Strategy Design for Value Creation
item.content:encoded:
Carmine Bianchi, University of Palermo

Greta Nasi, Bocconi University

Bin Chen, Baruch College

Gabriela Lotta, FGV-São Paulo School of Business Administration

Public administrations confront increasingly multifaceted challenges such as social inequality, climate change, and digital transformation that standard management approaches struggle to address. The call invites examination of how place-based strategy design can foster sustainable value creation by integrating organizational capabilities with local ecosystemic contexts, moving beyond traditional linear and centralized planning models toward adaptive, collaborative approaches grounded in specific spatial, cultural, and institutional conditions.

The special issue seeks contributions that advance understanding of how public value emerges from interactions between internal strategic intent and external community demands, mediated by place-specific factors termed locus and habitus. It emphasizes the need for performance management systems sensitive to local diversity, collaborative governance platforms, and methods that balance inside-out organizational perspectives with outside-in ecosystem thinking to address wicked problems effectively.

Appel publié par Public Management Review. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Frameworks for place-sensitive strategic planning in public services
  • How public value emerges within complex, nested ecosystems shaped by spatial and cultural dimensions of place
  • Methods for enhancing collaborative policy design and implementation in place-based ecosystems
  • The role of local knowledge, culture, and beliefs in shaping strategy
  • Interactions between inside-out (organizational) and outside-in (contextual) strategy perspectives
  • Synergies and tensions between internal capabilities and external demands in co-design of public service strategies
  • Adaptive and intelligent performance management systems
  • Indicators and metrics for value-in-context and value-in-society
  • The role of citizen perception in evaluating public service outcomes
  • How collaborative policymaking can generate value outcomes aligned with equity, accountability, transparency, trust, and social cohesion
  • The dynamics of value destruction in public service ecosystems
  • Collaborative platforms for cross-sector governance
  • Orchestration of theme-focused ecosystems for modular place development
  • Meta-governance and boundary-spanning leadership
  • Governance responses to turbulence and building robust place-based public services
  • Interplay of formal and informal knowledge in ecosystem adaptation
  • Digital platforms enabling citizen engagement and real-time data use
  • Role of AI and digital twins in place-based ecosystem visualization
